changes.summary: This is a review-only artifact specifying treatment and acceptance requirements. The required video, supporting files and publication must be implemented separately under the user's existing authorization; this verify artifact does not broker-deliver files.

decision: Adopt a hybrid course video: one locally produced 1080p H.264/AAC MP4 lasting 1800 seconds ±1 second, using Kokoro ONNX narration, Chromium-rendered teaching visuals and ffmpeg encoding. Preserve chapter starts at 00:00, 02:00, 06:00, 10:00, 13:00, 17:00, 21:00, 25:00 and 27:00, finishing at 30:00. Target approximately 27–29 minutes of narrated explanation, worked examples and answers. Allow at most three minutes of justified, announced practice—a ceiling, not a quota—with visible prompts, timers and subsequent answers; invite learners to pause playback for longer work. Fit speech through script revision against measured synthesized durations, without runtime padding or accelerated narration. Deliver synchronized WebVTT captions, an accessible timestamped transcript, chapter navigation and a public watch/download page through a separate versioned release. The existing HTML and narration probe do not establish completion of the video request. Final acceptance requires the source, encoded-media, accessibility and publication checks below.
dissent: No remaining material disagreement between the submitted positions. Final-video acceptance remains pending the required evidence; drafting does not establish exact-hash mutual ratification.

reasons: Continuous exposition simplifies timing and maximizes explanation, but provides less opportunity for the requested practice. A practice-heavy workshop supports active learning but leaves less narrated teaching time and assumes similar learner speeds.

The hybrid treatment preserves the established nine-chapter scope while combining explanation, short exercises and worked answers. Local narration feasibility supports this production route without establishing final-media quality.

Complete playback review, encoded-media checks and negative verification tests address failures that source assertions cannot detect. Separate versioned publication preserves the audited release and distinguishes new video evidence from historical HTML-course acceptance.
verify: Before scripting, read the complete docs/customer/course-source.json and its affected references, including results, CSV profiles, native-flow validation, loader/model explanation, runbook, upstream comparison, prediction record, quickstart, benchmark and export evidence. Check source bindings and hashes; investigate drift instead of refreshing expected values merely to pass. Create a requirement-to-source-to-narration-to-visual crosswalk and populate its final encoded-media timecodes after rendering. Keep unavailable evidence and unresolved content reviews explicitly pending.

Use the crosswalk to verify beginner explanations of packets versus flows; both uploaded packet CSVs versus validated native inputs; the six-class input/output contract; upstream code versus wrapper changes; functional pretraining versus paper pretraining; validation-selected fine-tuning and frozen inference; setup, tests and downloads; and customer teach-back with a worked answer. Source-check detailed pretraining counts, including the proposed 132-update description, before using them. Cover all audited reproduced results and documented protocol differences, explicitly including 91.26%, 84.05%, 84.63% and the 86.65% mean versus the paper's unreproduced 97.50%. Do not present a functional check as exact paper reproduction.

Verify the saved-error walkthrough against /predictions/635 and its class mapping: reference label 3, 1-Power-Other; predicted label 1, 6-Attacks-2-RTSP Brute Force; display score approximately 84.43%. Show and explain both labels, and distinguish display scores from calibrated confidence. Preserve recorded replay versus live IDS, model-only benchmarks versus operational throughput, the failed tested export path, and the absence of tested NPU/SmartNIC deployment. Introduce no new experimental results.

Record measured narration, practice and transition durations per chapter. Confirm that the script was fitted through revision and natural delivery, with every practice interval justified, announced, visibly labeled and followed by an answer. Total practice must not exceed 180 seconds. Declare bounded pause and transition windows in a machine-readable timeline before final acceptance; holds or silence introduced merely to reach 30 minutes fail the pacing gate.

Probe the final MP4 for H.264 video, AAC audio, 1920×1080 dimensions, valid timestamps, both streams spanning the intended programme and total duration of 1800 seconds ±1 second. Check embedded chapter markers against all nine prescribed offsets and inspect the actual audiovisual transitions within one second of those offsets. Completely decode both streams with ffmpeg and retain the error-free result; container metadata alone is insufficient.

Run silence detection on the final encoded audio with its parameters recorded. Reconcile every detected interval of at least three seconds against the bounded declared pause or transition windows. Extract frames from each such interval to confirm the corresponding prompt, timer or transition is actually visible. Investigate unexplained intervals and excessive cumulative gaps; do not excuse them through a retrospective manifest label.

Document an actual human review of the complete final playback against the crosswalk. Record reviewer identity, timecoded observations and corrections covering every reported result, the prediction error, all practice answers, chapter transitions, pronunciation, intelligibility, clipping and within-chapter audio/visual/caption alignment. Report measured loudness and peak/clipping results. Bind this review to the final MP4, WebVTT and transcript SHA-256 hashes. If the human review has not occurred, leave that gate pending.

Validate WebVTT syntax and cue timing against the media duration. Compare captions with encoded speech within 0.5 seconds at each chapter's first utterance and distributed samples throughout every chapter, alongside the complete playback review. Inspect every teaching scene at desktop and phone full-screen playback sizes for legibility and caption obstruction. Speak or describe essential visual information. Verify a reflowing timestamped transcript, keyboard-operable playback and chapter navigation, and same-origin caption loading through the published watch page.

Demonstrate that the new automated verification gates reject truncated media, missing audio, silent audio, invalid caption timing and checksum mismatches. Run the existing static-course verification and relevant regression checks, retaining commands and results. Maintain a separate revision-specific video receipt with final asset hashes, source/render/publishing revisions, narration engine/model/voice identity, crosswalk, measured checks and actual review outcomes. Do not inherit static-course pass statuses; changed assets require renewed affected checks.

Before public distribution, review redistribution terms for the new visuals and voice outputs. Preserve the existing disclosure that inherited asset terms remain unresolved, and do not bundle raw datasets or model weights. Publish the video and supporting downloads in a separate versioned release with latest promotion explicitly disabled, using make_latest=false or its equivalent. Record before/after verification that customer-2026-09-15-audited still resolves to its original commit identified as 17b4aae, all seven original attachment hashes are unchanged, and releases/latest retains its original destination. Verify the separately listed protected_artifacts hashes without treating them as the seven release attachments.

Verify anonymous downloads of the published MP4, captions and transcript against their recorded hashes. Test the public watch page for playback, seeking near the end, chapter navigation, captions and usable download links. Record the actual public URLs and publishing revision. Update current entry points honestly to identify the newly added video, using a separate video manifest and receipt where needed to preserve protected records. Do not rewrite historical council fd14aca3-fea0-499a-9fe2-167ae5182876 or static-course provenance as having delivered video.

Record a real content review of the affected lesson sources and references. Inspect the applicable pending-content-reviews.json and video-refresh-queue.json entries without changing the separately owned worker or shared state; leave unresolved reviews visible and do not clear baselines without review. Keep implementation within this course: no new training experiments, Claude bulk video refresh, or changes to unrelated courses or policy.
